statement_summary: Security Coordinator designated in writing
Annual risk assessment with SP 800-30; risks owned and treated
Risk acceptance authority; High risks never accepted
Sanctions recorded; good-faith reporting protected
Vendor approval: confidentiality terms, U.S. storage, client authorization
Annual independent evaluation
Five-year retention of security records
Annual policy review; policies available to staff
Written, risk-rated, time-limited exceptions
Named accounts only; entries@ as a shared mailbox; shared portal passwords only in the password manager
Role-based least privilege with written approval; 2 platform administrators
MFA everywhere including MSP-held administrator logins; number matching
Termination checklist by the last day; CBP update within 10 days; signing authority withdrawal
Monthly account reconciliation; quarterly role check
10-minute screen lock
Named MSP and vendor accounts with MFA; yearly technician list
Password length; no spreadsheets; default passwords changed before use
Company mail on phones only through protected suite apps
Call-back and dual approval for new or changed payees
Monthly log review; external tag and impersonation protection
Client records confidential; need-to-know access
No client records in personal accounts, messaging apps, or public AI tools
Lock screens; never share passwords or MFA codes
Security training at hire and yearly; phishing simulations
Report suspected incidents and odd payment requests at once
Signed policy acknowledgment
BEC runbook kept and printed
Report suspected incidents within 1 hour
Bank fraud line first for a suspect wire; IC3 complaint the same day
Log every incident and near-miss
CBP Security Operations Center notice within 72 hours with compromised importer numbers; 10-business-day update
Florida breach determination documented; notices meet the P08 matrix
Insurer hotline first; MSP engaged under contract
Ransom or extortion payment only with approvals and an OFAC check
Vendor incident reports within 10 days logged and handled
Annual tabletop with the MSP and the bank fraud process
Lessons learned within 30 days
Three classification levels; customs records Restricted
Encrypt Restricted data at rest and in transit
Restricted data only in approved systems with U.S. storage
Inventory and importer number data map
New tools and vendor-enabled features approved before receiving Restricted data
Approved AI tools only; broker approval of new AI classifications
Scanned records only after the 163.5 notice, under a written procedure, with a yearly retrieval test
Daily backup, 1-year undeletable versions; quarterly restore test
Retention: 5 years for customs, forwarder, and export records; POA rule; no deletion of records sought
Wipe or certified destruction with records
